newsitem.title: USA: Democrats pick up three seats in Washington state.
newsitem.headline: Democrats pick up three seats in Washington state.

text.p: Washington state voters, who gave Republicans one of their biggest 1994 victories, sent three of six freshmen congressmen packing in Tuesday's election, according to results Wednesday.
Democrats will have five of the state's nine seats in the next Congress, up from just two currently.

In the mostly suburban Ninth District south of Seattle, state Sen. Adam Smith defeated Randy Tate, the youngest member of the 1994 Republican freshman class, by a 53 to 47 percent margin with 73 percent of precincts reporting.

In another closely watched race in a suburban Seattle swing district, Republican Rick White kept his seat for a second term, narrowly defeating fellow former prosecutor Jeff Coopersmith by 52 to 48 percent.

But Republican Linda Smith lost to psychologist and political newcomer Brian Baird by a slender 4,000-vote margin. With 81 percent of the vote counted in southeast Washington's Third District, Democrat Baird had a 51 to 49 percent lead, and CNN declared him the winner.
Smith, who made campaign finance reform her cornerstone issue, said she thought early returns broadcast from the East Coast might have discouraged some of her supporters from going to the polls.

Jack Metcalf, the oldest member of the freshmen class, lost to state Sen. Kevin Quigley by an even narrower 2,500-vote margin, CNN said. Quigley had 49 percent of the total, compared with 48 percent for Metcalf, with the rest going to a third-party candidate.

George Nethercutt, who toppled former House Speaker Tom Foley in 1994, easily beat wheat farmer Judy Olson in eastern Washington's vast Fifth District. And Republican Doc Hastings won a second term over Rick Locke in central Washington's Fourth District.
